I will keep things simple and steady this year. I am 68, so I do not want a crop plan that is too scattered or too labor-heavy. In Quzhou, the land and weather fit the usual wheat-maize rotation well, and I trust that system because it is familiar, easy to manage, and gives me grain from two seasons on the same land. I will keep most of my land in winter wheat followed by summer maize. That way I use the land fully, spread risk across the year, and do not need to learn a new crop. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because they usually stand better and yield more reliably. I will fertilize moderately, not too heavily, because fertilizer is expensive and too much can lodge the crop or waste money. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat needs water at key stages in spring here, while maize can often get by with fewer waterings if the summer rain is normal. I will plough before wheat and use rotary tillage before maize to save effort and time after the wheat harvest. I will spray only as needed, mainly for common diseases, weeds, and insects, because I want to protect yield but keep costs and work under control.
